params.body:
Ilse switched both modules off for M.I. Cars, removed his vehicles and his login, and the iframe on
micars.be/catalogus still served our catalogue from traders.stocklistdealer.eu. It answered 200.

`website/{dealer_hash}` decrypted the hash, found the dealer and rendered. It checked nothing else,
so the embed kept working for as long as a former customer left the snippet in his page.

His was empty, which is the mild version. The widget can show the shared stocklist instead of the
dealer's own stock (`default_all_vehicles`, or the visitor flipping the toggle), and then a former
customer keeps publishing other dealers' cars on his own website. Nothing in the code stopped that,
and nothing would have reported it, because the page answered 200 either way.

So the embed now follows the package: with `module_1` and `module_2` both off, every public entry
point answers 410 with one neutral sentence, no branding and no logo, because that page renders
inside somebody else's site and putting our mark there is worse than the empty list it replaces.

Two choices worth naming:

- The check is middleware on the whole route group, not a guard in the controller. There are ten
  public entry points into `WebsiteController` and the eleventh would be added without it.
- It refuses only what it is sure about. A hash that will not decrypt, or one that points at no
  dealer, is passed through exactly as before: this is a gate on a package, not a second opinion on
  everything that can be wrong with a URL. A test pins that.

Run against the routes currently on main, the new test reports the live situation: "Expected
response status code [410] but received 200."

Note for the merge: this takes effect for every dealer with both modules off, not only M.I. Cars.
params.title: The embed on a dealer's own site follows his package
